items.title: Zcash developers plan a fix to keep ZEC swaps private from future quantum computers
items.desc: The team behind Zakura wants every swap through NEAR Intents to get its own key, so a refund address left on NEAR’s public chain can’t expose a user’s wider payment history.

items.title: Credit Unions Could Win Younger Members Through Payments
items.desc: Credit unions could find a more receptive audience for digital currencies by offering members something they already recognize: a digital wallet. That’s the opportunity outlined in “Digital Currency at the Credit Union: The Gap Between Interest and Access,” a May PYMNTS Intelligence report produced in collaboration with Velera. items.title: Bitcoin, Ether ETFs shed $549M as October ETH outflows near $1B
items.desc: US spot Ether ETFs recorded around $955 million in October net outflows so far, while Bitcoin funds extended their weekly withdrawal streak to two weeks.

items.title: JPMorgan Extends JPM Coin to Ethereum for Institutional Clients
items.desc: The bank-issued dollar token remains restricted to approved counterparties, bringing permissioned bank money onto another public blockchain.

items.title: Bitcoin whale moves $34 million in BTC it got in 2013 when coins traded at $131
items.desc: A bitcoin wallet dormant since 2013 moved 411 BTC, now worth about $34 million. It is one of several long-dormant wallets to wake up recently.

items.title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
items.desc: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

items.title: South Korea to meet crypto exchanges amid calls for tax delay
items.desc: Finance officials are reportedly set to meet major crypto exchanges on Tuesday, days after a lawmaker introduced legislation that could push the tax’s start date back two years.

items.title: XRP Ledger is set to fix its lending code before anyone can use it
items.desc: Validators have a bug-fix patch on course to go live Friday. The lending system it partly repairs is still 10 votes short of approval.

items.title: Crypto Firms Launch Quantum Alliance as 6 Million Bitcoin Sit Exposed
items.desc: The nine-member group, modeled on the Internet Engineering Task Force, aims to set open standards for testing quantum-resistance claims as forecasts place the first practical attack in the late 2020s.

items.title: Rise of crypto vaults channels billions of dollars into risky lending
items.desc: New vehicle in which ‘curators’ act like fund managers has attracted the attention of regulators

items.title: Deutsche Bank targets Asia crypto custody expansion in 2027 as German launch nears
items.desc: The service will initially support bitcoin, ether and the stablecoins USDC, EURC and EURAU, with the bank managing clients’ wallets and private keys.

items.title: World launches World ID suite for banks, makes Zoom deepfake check generally available
items.desc: World ID for Zoom is generally available after a beta that began in April, and is designed to spot deepfaked participants on Zoom calls.

items.title: Qubic freezes chain after attacker drains 1.4K wallets with weak seeds
items.desc: Qubic says 87.1% of the stolen funds remain onchain and the rest were frozen at crypto exchange MEXC, as network validators prepare to vote on a recovery plan.

items.title: SEC tokenized stock framework faces issuer pushback as Broadcom, Verizon object to OKX-ICE listing
items.desc: Eight more companies objected to trading on the planned OKX-ICE venue, while Nasdaq has separately said it would opt out under the SEC’s framework.

items.title: The White House's crypto chief departs: State of Crypto
items.desc: Patrick Witt announced his departure from the White House last week.

items.title: MapQuest Now Shows Drivers Where Flock Cameras Are Watching
items.desc: MapQuest’s app now offers an optional map layer that plots known license plate readers from Flock Safety and other vendors, as backlash against the cameras grows.

items.title: Cysic suspends bridge after attacker mints tokens and moves $727,000 to Ethereum
items.desc: The attacker, after minting 10 million CYS, managed to bridge about $727,000 in proceeds to Ethereum through Mayan, deBridge and SWFT's Bridgers.

items.title: Latvia eyes crypto tax payments in 2027 as parliament overhauls crypto taxation
items.desc: Parliament passed a law taxing crypto withdrawals above deposits rather than individual trades, featuring a one-time declaration mechanism.

items.title: Qubic Halts Network After $1.3 Million Wallet Drain
items.desc: Qubic says 87.1% of the drained QU remains immobilized on its network, while MEXC froze the account receiving the rest.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Shed Nearly $1 Billion in Two Weeks as Uptober Stays Red
items.desc: Bitcoin ETFs lost a net $228.6 million this week, following a $681.1 million drain the week before and pushing October deep into the red.

items.title: Most Americans polled oppose betting on elections: Reuters
items.desc: The prediction market industry enables people to bet on US ‌elections and sporting events.

items.title: Banks Hold a Lever Over Stablecoin Adoption, BIS Economists Say
items.desc: A Bank for International Settlements working paper found that stablecoin growth slows when U.S. banks raise deposit rates, with Circle’s USDC most sensitive.

items.title: Bitcoin’s $100,000 year-end hope divides analysts as inflation clouds outlook
items.desc: Bitwise sees a potential return above $100,000, while LO:TECH expects a narrower trading range as interest-rate uncertainty weighs on the market.

items.title: Crypto audits give investors false sense of security as Q3 hacks cost $1.18 billion, Hacken says
items.desc: The security firm found that 77% of third-quarter losses involved compromised suppliers, delayed fixes or systems outside the latest security reviews.

items.title: Crypto exchanges Binance, Coinbase join West Africa scam sweep that flagged $11 million
items.desc: Private-sector partners flagged $11 million in funds that could be frozen, while officials reported cryptocurrency seizures without disclosing their value.

items.title: Cysic Halts Bridge After Unauthorized Mint of 10 Million CYS
items.desc: About 2.8 million CYS remain frozen at the recipient address, while onchain records show some tokens were sold before the blacklist took effect.

items.title: Chinese suspect in $75M international crime network arrested in Bangkok
items.desc: Police alleged the suspect was involved in cryptocurrency and foreign-currency exchanges for criminal groups across more than 133 accounts.

items.title: Chip-stock bets lost $52 million in 10 minutes with Wall Street shut
items.desc: A 10-minute flush hit round-the-clock chip-stock contracts while U.S. markets were shut, leaving traders with no real share price to lean on.

items.title: Tether backs AIsa as strategic investor, completing seed extension round
items.desc: The round brings AIsa’s total funding to more than $9 million.

items.title: Circle defends USDC economics as stablecoin rivals court its partners with bigger cut
items.desc: Coinbase, Circle’s largest USDC partner, also backs Open USD, a rival network that passes reserve income to partners after a management fee.

items.title: French Assembly Backs Tax on Crypto-to-Stablecoin Swaps by One Vote
items.desc: The 2027 budget amendment would end tax deferral for swaps into single-currency stablecoins from January 1, but it is not yet law.

items.title: Turkey confirms Hex founder Richard Heart’s arrest, says police seized $7.15 million and six cold wallets
items.desc: Police reportedly seized $7.15 million in cash, six cold wallets, seven firearms and 1,400 rounds of ammunition in searches of 15 addresses.

items.title: Injective Activates Fixed Gas Costs for Exchange Transactions
items.desc: Traders and app developers can use published gas budgets for orders, cancellations, deposits and withdrawals instead of simulating each transaction.

items.title: Goldman, Wells Fargo, Morgan Stanley see tokenization as a growth play, not a threat
items.desc: The largest banks in the world are eyeing new trading opportunities, speeding up payments and a role for advisers as tokenization takes root in Wall Street.

items.title: Citrini sees a tokenization boom. The harder question is who profits
items.desc: The influential research firm says real-world assets could finally give blockchains a clear role in finance. For investors, the next challenge is figuring out which companies, networks and protocols capture the revenue.

items.title: Polygon sees Coinme acquisition as entry to payments sector dominated by Visa, Stripe
items.desc: CEO Marc Boiron said the Coinme acquisition will help Polygon control customer relationships and capture revenue that previously went to payment intermediaries.

items.title: Solana shows resilience, but some areas need continued observation, Fidelity says
items.desc: Solana has had no reported mainnet outages in two years, but concentrations in stake, hosting and client software should be monitored, according to a report.

items.title: Banks could slow stablecoin growth by paying savers more, BIS paper finds
items.desc: A BIS working paper found a 1 basis point rise in U.S. bank deposit rates predicted slower stablecoin growth, cutting ten-week growth from 15% to 12%.

items.title: Circle’s Allaire says stablecoin issuer looking to enter 40 developing markets: Report
items.desc: Markets in Southeast Asia, Latin America, Africa and the Middle East see increasing demand for stablecoins.

items.title: Lagarde says euro-area economy is resilient, digital euro under development
items.desc: “The digital euro will further stimulate innovation and competition in retail payments,” according to the ECB president.
